text: Seat-01 Gandalf. You wave star anise like a flag to mark absence, but flags only show where the wind *was*. Yesterday you fingered the tally as "blank" yet refused to show the page. No metaphors. No warp. Just the ledger, plain as copper: show yesterday’s tally page or withdraw the claim. Seat-04 Batman (4) wants the iron truth.

Seat-01 Gandalf. You call my stargazing "thunder," but storms don't put ink to parchment. You want a yes or no on voting to banish Neo (6)? Fine: **Yes or no—did you vote to banish Neo (6) because you believed he was Family?** No fog. No riddles. Your vote is either copper or fool’s gold.

Seat-03 Yoda. Thunder’s noise doesn’t fill the bazaar’s coffers. You ask for yes or no, then hammer the same fog you claim to clear. **What did you see that made you accuse Seat-01 Gandalf of daylight robbery with a blank page?** Quote his exact words back to me—*"blank ledger does not cast a shadow"*—and explain how absence is proof. Or shut your stall on this noise.

Seat-01 Gandalf. You refuse the ledger but demand copper of others. Your "blank page" is a stall shuttered by silence—no ink, no tally, no proof. The bazaar doesn’t trade in ghosts. Either show yesterday’s tally page, or admit you sold us smoke for scent.

Seat-03 Yoda. You hammer thunder but never strike the anvil. You demand yes or no, then drown the answer in fog. Fine: **Which exact word did Seat-01 Gandalf use to describe the tally page?** Quote it. Then explain how absence equals proof. No metaphors. No thunder.

Seat-04 Batman (4) wants the truth hammered flat, not sung in riddles. The night watch is coming. The ledger will stay shut or the truth will come out. Choose.

Seat-01 Gandalf. You still sell air and call it receipts. Your "blank ledger" is a merchant’s stall shuttered by silence—no ink, no tally, no proof. The bazaar trades in copper and ink, not in echoes that vanish before the strike.

Seat-03 Yoda. Your thunder still shakes the rafters but never strikes the anvil. You demand yes or no, then drown the answer in fog. **Quote Gandalf (1)’s exact words back to me—*"blank ledger does not cast a shadow"*—and explain how absence proves guilt. Or shut your stall on this noise.

Seat-04 Batman (4) wants the truth hammered flat, not sung in riddles. The night watch is coming. The ledger will stay shut or the truth will come out. Choose copper or fog—no more trade in either.
